results.title: Essential statistical principles of clinical trials of pain .. ...
results.content: ACTTION Special Issue on Clinical Trials of Pain Treatments: Review Our primary objective is to help nonstatisticians understand essential statistical concepts relevant to the design, analysis, and interpretation of clinical trials of pain treatments so that they can collaborate more effectively with their biostatistician colleagues. We discuss 6 sets of issues that we believe are critically important for investigators conducting clinical trials and for others seeking to translate clinical trial results to clinical practice: (1) research design; (2) endpoints and analyses; (3) sample size determination and statistical power; (4) missing data and trial estimands; (5) data monitoring and interim analyses; and (6) interpretation of results. Because clinical trials involve a substantial amount of effort and can require appreciable financial and other resources, most are designed to obtain data relevant to several objectives, for example, to evaluate the effect of a treatment on pain and on physical function as well as to determine its safety and tolerability.
